scope: Second search: non-party organisations that helped electors during the SIR in the states where the first search (orgs.json) found nothing. Nothing in orgs.json is repeated. Every quote was checked on 2026-10-09 against the page fetched from source_url.

organisations.name: Tamil Nadu Thowheed Jamath (TNTJ), Tiruchy and Madurai units
organisations.what: Ran SIR help camps in at least 30 mosques in Tiruchy during enumeration. Volunteers searched the 2002 and 2005 rolls, checked people's details and helped them fill their forms. The Madurai branches trained office-bearers across 36 units.
organisations.quote: In Tiruchy, Tamil Nadu Thowheed Jamath (TNTJ) has set up camps in at least 30 mosques. Volunteers, who have downloaded PDFs of the 2002 and 2005 voter rolls, entered the details into Excel sheets, verify data and help people in filling SIR forms.
organisations.notes: A religious organisation, not a party. The same report names party-run camps (MMK, MJK, IUML), which are listed under excluded_parties. The organisation said it planned to check the draft roll and file claims; no report of that later work was found. Its website (tntj.net) refused the fetch, so how_to_reach is blank.

organisations.name: Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Coimbatore district unit
organisations.what: Ran SIR help camps on weekday evenings and full days at weekends in five Coimbatore localities (Podanur, Karumbukadai, GM Nagar, Saramedu and Kuniyamuthur) during enumeration.
organisations.quote: In Coimbatore, the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind is conducts camps in the evenings on week days and full-day camps on the weekend in Podanur, Karumbukadai, GM Nagar, Saramedu and Kuniyamuthur.
organisations.notes: Quote is verbatim, including the paper's typo "is conducts". Jamaat-e-Islami Hind is a religious organisation, not a party; it has been linked in press reports to political parties elsewhere (Welfare Party of India), which is worth knowing but is not a party role here. No national or state SIR programme by the organisation was found.

organisations.name: Vallakkadavu mosque (jamaath) committee, Thiruvananthapuram
organisations.what: Set up one of the first SIR help desks in Kerala in the first week of November 2025, open to the public as well as its own members, and filled in enumeration forms after finding people's names in the 2002 roll. Hundreds had used it within two weeks.
organisations.quote: It set up a help desk in the first week of November, urging mahal members as well as the public to seek its assistance in filling the enumeration form.
organisations.notes: Also verbatim in the same report: "the initiative was getting a good response and hundreds of people had so far sought their service" and "For such people, we filled their forms after finding their names in the 2002 voters list". Both are attributed to a named office-bearer, who is not named here.

organisations.name: Mosque committees of Balaramapuram town mosque and Chemboor mosque (Thiruvananthapuram), Panavally Thekkum Bhagam mosque (Alappuzha) and Badriya Masjid (Chavakkad, Thrissur)
organisations.what: Followed Vallakkadavu in setting up teams of volunteers to help the public complete the SIR enumeration form.
organisations.quote: Soon, several other committees - notable among them being Balaramapuram town mosque, Chemboor mosque in Thiruvananthapuram, Panavally Thekkum Bhagam mosque in Alappuzha and Badriya Masjid in Chavakkad -   followed suit and set up dedicated teams of volunteers to help the public complete the formality.
organisations.notes: Four separate committees in one entry because the source names them in one sentence and gives no figures for any of them. Split them if the page lists organisations one per row. The quote keeps the source's spacing before "followed".

organisations.name: Edappally Mahallu Muslim Jama-ath committee, Kochi
organisations.what: Ran an SIR help desk during the revision, one of the earliest in Kochi. The Cochin Diocese later cited the Mahallu committees' help desks as the model for its own drive.
organisations.quote: the helpdesk that it set up, one of the earliest during the SIR, had turned out to be highly effective
organisations.notes: The quote is a fragment; the full sentence names a committee office-bearer. The effectiveness claim is the committee's own. The same article says, in the paper's voice: "The Church has apparently taken a cue from help desks organised by community groups, especially Muslim Mahallu committees, during the SIR process." The committee said it saw no need for a campaign after the SIR.

organisations.name: Diocese of Cochin (Roman Catholic)
organisations.what: After the SIR, launched a door-to-door drive by trained youth volunteers to find people left off the roll or never enrolled, across about 40,750 families in four Assembly constituencies, with help desks for people of all communities to enrol (Form 6). At least 3,000 people had been identified within the first week.
organisations.quote: At least 3,000 such people have already been identified during the drive, the Church leaders involved in the campaign said.
organisations.notes: The 3,000 is the diocese's own figure, and it counts people identified, not enrolled. The help desks are described in the future tense in the article; the door-to-door visits had begun. The website is the diocese's own site, which loaded on 2026-10-09; it was not checked for an SIR page.

organisations.name: Catholic Association of Goa, with the parish pastoral councils of the Church in Goa
organisations.what: During enumeration, parish pastoral council members were each put in charge of 35 to 40 households, visited them when the BLOs came, and checked the forms had been filled and the names kept on the roll. The councils said they would watch the draft roll's deletions and help get names restored.
organisations.quote: We were tasked to visit houses when the BLOs came and cross-check if they had done all the formalities properly and their names included in the roll.
organisations.notes: The account is given by an office-bearer of the Catholic Association of Goa, so it is the organisation's own description. Also verbatim: "each church has a parish council or PPC which has around seven to eight PPC members, and each member was put in charge of 35-40 houses". Mainly for Catholic households; the source does not say others were served. The desktop URL (thewire.in/rights/...) renders no article text without JavaScript, so the m.thewire.in address is given.

organisations.name: Masjid-e-Teenposh and Imdadul Uloom Madrasa, Red Hills, Hyderabad
organisations.what: Volunteers at the mosque and its madrasa filled and uploaded SIR applications online for residents, free of charge, where internet centres were charging Rs 100 to 200 a form.
organisations.quote: Masjid-e-Teenposh in Hyderabad's Red Hills is helping residents complete Special Intensive Revision (SIR) applications for electoral rolls free of cost.
organisations.notes: OUTSIDE THE ASKED STATES: Telangana was covered by the first search, but this organisation is not in orgs.json, so it is added. Drop it if the second list must keep to the states named.

excluded_parties.name: Manithaneya Makkal Katchi (MMK), ward camps in Tiruchy and Sunday camps in Ambur, Tamil Nadu
Manithaneya Jananayaga Katchi (MJK), 40+ camps and a Chennai SIR helpline, Tamil Nadu
Indian Union Muslim League, about 1,000 volunteers across 52 district units, Tamil Nadu
SDPI, enumeration form help desk, Kundgol, Karnataka

not_found: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Haryana, Punjab, Puducherry, Uttarakhand and the North-East (Meghalaya, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, Arunachal, Sikkim): no named non-party organisation shown delivering help. Reports name only government camps and help desks, party booth agents, and advocacy (memoranda, protests).

Bihar beyond the Legal Services Authority: none found, in English, Hindi or Urdu. Imarat-e-Shariah, Jamiat, Bharat Jodo Abhiyan and Jan Jagran Shakti Sangathan were each searched by name; the last ran a public hearing on the SIR (The Wire, 2025-07-21), which is testimony, not help.
Uttar Pradesh beyond Ghazipur: mosque and madrasa help camps in Bijnor, Meerut and Muzaffarnagar districts are reported, but no organisation is named (see left_out).
Jharkhand: two Muslim organisations announced help (see left_out); no report of help delivered.
Legal Services Authorities: no SIR help desk or legal aid service found in any state other than Bihar's court-directed one, in English or Hindi (विधिक सेवा प्राधिकरण, पैरा लीगल).
Searches in Gujarati, Odia and Punjabi returned nothing on the SIR from Google News; Telugu returned only Telangana government and party desks.

Arunachal Pradesh: the Chakma Development Foundation of India complained to the Commission and the NHRC about Chakma electors kept from hearings (August to September 2026). That is advocacy, not help with hearings, and the article URL was not resolved, so it is not listed.

left_out.name: Indian Cultural Foundation (ICF), Oman National Committee: 51 SIR help desks for Kerala expatriates (Form 6A)
left_out.why: The report (Suprabhaatham, 2025-12-13) announces the desks opening that day; no report of help delivered was found. ICF is a Kerala Muslim Jamaath affiliate, not a party.

left_out.name: Jharkhand Tanzeem, SIR help centre and helpline, Ranchi
left_out.why: ETV Bharat (2026-05-11) reports the centre's inauguration and a planned awareness tour, before the Jharkhand SIR began. Its later appearance (2026-09-22) is a memorandum to the CEO. No help delivered is shown.

left_out.name: Imarat-e-Shariah, training of youth for SIR help in Jharkhand
left_out.why: A plan (January to February 2026 training tour) with no report that it ran.

left_out.name: Mosques and madrasas in Bijnor, Meerut and Muzaffarnagar districts, Uttar Pradesh
left_out.why: The Times of India (2025-11-25) describes help camps in Sherkot, Nagina, Dhampur and Najibabad but names no organisation; the one named institution, an Islamia madrasa in Nagina, ran a desk 'supported by a local MLA'.

left_out.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace, Purvanchal (UP) team
left_out.why: Pages 41 to 46 record case studies and a BLO interview in Varanasi and Azamgarh; they document problems and show no help given.

left_out.name: Asom Mojuri Sramik Union, Banchana Birudhi Mancha and Forum for Social Harmony (Assam)
left_out.why: Named on page 35 only as co-signatories of CJP's memorandum to the Commission. No other trace of the three names was found, so their nature and any party links could not be checked.
